title: The courts
note: Drafted for Prompt 12 (Unit 2). Every lesson is a draft until a person reviews it (content/course/README.md).

listen.explanationKey: What is the highest court in the United States?
facts: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States.
The Supreme Court and the other federal courts are the judicial branch.

newWords.meaning: a place where judges decide questions about the law
the highest court in the United States

story.say: The Supreme Court is the highest court in the United States.

help.simpler: No court is higher than the Supreme Court.
help.example: The Supreme Court works in this building in Washington, D.C.
help.why: The test asks for the highest court. The answer is the Supreme Court.

story.say: It is at the top of the judicial branch.

help.simpler: The Supreme Court is above all the other federal courts.
help.example: Think of steps: the other federal courts are below, the Supreme Court is at the top.
help.why: Knowing it is at the top helps you remember “highest court.”

story.say: The Supreme Court and the other federal courts are the judicial branch.

help.simpler: All the federal courts together make up the judicial branch.
help.example: There are federal courts in every state, and the Supreme Court in Washington, D.C.
help.why: The test asks for one part of the judicial branch: the Supreme Court or the federal courts.

check.prompt: Which one is part of the judicial branch?

readIt.sentence: What is the capital of the United States?

writeIt.sentence: Washington, D.C. is the capital of the United States.

listen.explanationKey: What does the judicial branch do?
facts: They decide disagreements about the law, and if a law goes against the Constitution.

newWords.meaning: to choose someone for a job
when courts decide if a law goes against the Constitution
when the Senate votes yes on a person the President chose

help.simpler: Courts look closely at laws and say what they mean.
help.example: If people read a law in two different ways, a court explains what it means.
help.why: “Reviews laws” and “Explains laws” are answers about what the judicial branch does.

story.say: They decide disagreements about the law.

help.simpler: When people disagree about the law, a court decides.
help.example: Two businesses argue about a contract. A court decides who is right under the law.
help.why: “Resolves disputes about the law” is another answer on the test.

story.say: Courts also decide if a law goes against the Constitution.

help.simpler: A court can say a law breaks the Constitution. Then the law cannot be used.
help.example: This is called judicial review. It is how the courts check Congress and the President.
help.why: “Decides if a law goes against the Constitution” is another answer on the test.

help.example: The Senate must confirm, or agree, before a judge starts the job.
help.why: The test asks who appoints federal judges. The answer is the President.

readIt.sentence: What is one right in the Bill of Rights?

writeIt.sentence: Freedom of speech is one right.

listen.explanationKey: How many seats are on the Supreme Court?
facts: The Supreme Court has nine seats.
Usually five justices are needed to decide a case.

newWords.meaning: a judge on the Supreme Court

story.say: The Supreme Court has nine seats.

help.simpler: Nine justices sit on the Supreme Court.
help.example: A justice is a judge on the Supreme Court.
help.why: The test asks how many seats are on the Supreme Court. The answer is nine.

story.say: Each seat is for one justice.

help.simpler: A “seat” is a place for one justice.
help.example: When a seat opens, the President chooses someone new, and the Senate must agree.

check.prompt: How many seats are on the Supreme Court?

story.say: Usually five justices are needed to decide a case.

help.simpler: A case is decided when at least five of the nine agree.
help.example: If five justices agree and four disagree, the five decide the case.
help.why: The test asks how many justices are usually needed to decide a case. The answer is five.

check.prompt: How many justices are usually needed to decide a case?

readIt.sentence: How many Senators does Congress have?

listen.explanationKey: How long do Supreme Court justices serve?
facts: Supreme Court justices serve for life, until they retire.
Serving for life helps them stay independent of politics.

story.say: Supreme Court justices serve for life.

help.simpler: Once a justice joins the Supreme Court, there is no end date.
help.example: A justice can serve for many years, sometimes 30 years or more.
help.why: The test asks how long justices serve. The answer is for life.

story.say: A justice can stay until they choose to retire.

help.simpler: They keep the job until they decide to stop.
help.example: “Retire” means to stop working, often when someone is older.
help.why: “Until retirement” is another answer on the test.

check.statement: Supreme Court justices serve for four years.

story.say: Serving for life helps them stay independent of politics.

help.simpler: They do not have to worry about losing their job, so they can decide freely.
help.example: A justice does not need to win an election, so they can make decisions many people dislike.
help.why: The test asks why justices serve for life. “To be independent of politics” is one answer.

story.say: They can decide cases without worrying about the next election.

help.simpler: Justices do not run for office, so elections do not change their decisions.
help.example: A justice can say what the law means, even if many people disagree.
help.why: “To limit outside political influence” is the other answer on the test.

check.prompt: Why do Supreme Court justices serve for life?

readIt.sentence: Why do people come to America?

listen.explanationKey: Who is the Chief Justice of the United States now?
facts: The Chief Justice leads the Supreme Court.
This name changes only when a Chief Justice leaves the job, so Pathways looks it up on an official list.
Check the names again before your interview.

newWords.meaning: the leader of the Supreme Court

story.say: The Chief Justice leads the Supreme Court.

help.simpler: The Chief Justice is the head of the Supreme Court.
help.example: In the picture, the Chief Justice sits in the middle.
help.why: The test asks for the name of the Chief Justice now.

story.say: This is the Chief Justice today.

help.simpler: The name under the picture is the Chief Justice now.
help.example: Officer: “Who is the Chief Justice now?” You say the name shown here.
help.why: Use the name from this official list for the test.

story.say: This name can change, so the app looks it up on an official list.

help.simpler: A new Chief Justice is chosen when the last one leaves the job.
help.example: The President chooses a new Chief Justice, and the Senate agrees.
help.why: This way you always learn the right name.

story.say: Check the name again before your interview.

help.simpler: Look at the name one more time close to your interview day.
help.example: It does not change often, but it is good to check.
help.why: You want to give the name of the Chief Justice on your interview day.

readIt.sentence: Who has the right to vote?

writeIt.sentence: Citizens have the right to vote.
